chunks: A group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was with Aisha one night, so he arose to pray the optional prayer. Aisha woke up and struck with her hand but did not find him, so she thought that he had gone to her slave girl. She stood up and circled around him, and she trampled upon his neck (peace be upon him and his family) while he was prostrating, weeping.

He was saying: 'My dark garments and my views prostrate to You, and my heart believes in You. I acknowledge to You the blessings, and I confess to You the great sin; I did evil and wronged myself, so forgive me. Indeed, none forgives the great sin except You.'

I seek refuge with Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge with Your pleasure from Your anger, and I seek refuge with Your mercy from Your wrath, and I seek refuge with You from You. I cannot fully reach Your praise and eulogy upon You; You are as You have praised Yourself. I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You.'
So when he finished, he said: 'O Aisha! You have caused pain to my neck. What did you fear, that I would stand up to go to your slave girl?'

key_terms.سَوَادِي: My dark garments (referring to the dark color of the Prophet's clothing)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say while prostrating when Aisha stepped on his neck?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Prophet’s profound humility and devotion during voluntary night prayers, illustrating the Shia emphasis on *Tahajjud* as a means of spiritual refinement. The detailed supplication recited while prostrate underscores the concept of *Istighfar* (seeking forgiveness) and reliance on divine mercy, a theme central to Shia devotional practices. Aisha’s gentle interruption serves as a narrative device to reveal the depth of the Prophet’s introspection, reinforcing the scholarly view that even the infallible Prophet engaged in continuous self-accountability.

en.hubeali:
A group of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allahsaww was with Ayesha one night, and hesaww arose to pray the Optional Salāt. So Ayesha woke up and she struck by her hand, but did not find himsaww. So she thought that heasws had gone to her slave girl. So she stood up circling upon himsaww and she trampled upon hissaww neck, and hesaww was prostrating, weeping,

saying: ‘Isaww perform Sajdah to Yousaww in mysaww mourning garments and mysaww views, and Isaww believe in Youazwj with mysaww heart acknowledging to Youazwj of mysaww Blessings, and acknowledging to Youazwj with the great sin, evil deed and being unjust to myselfsaww’ (on behalf of mysaww nation). Therefore, Forgive myasws (nation) there being no Forgiver of the great sins except for Youazwj.

I<sup>saww</sup> hereby seek Refuge with Your<sup>azwj</sup> Pardoning, and I<sup>saww</sup> seek Refuge with Your<sup>azwj</sup> Pleasure from Your<sup>azwj</sup> Anger, and I<sup>saww</sup> seek Refuge with Your<sup>azwj</sup> Mercy from Your<sup>azwj</sup> Curse, and I<sup>saww</sup> seek Refuge with You<sup>azwj</sup> from You<sup>azwj</sup>. I<sup>saww</sup> cannot deservingly deliver Your<sup>azwj</sup> Praise and Laudation upon You<sup>azwj</sup> . You<sup>azwj</sup> are as You<sup>azwj</sup> Praised upon Yourself<sup>saww</sup>. I seek Forgiveness from You<sup>azwj</sup> and I<sup>saww</sup> turn to You<sup>azwj</sup>’.
So when he<sup>saww</sup> finished, said: ‘O Ayesha! You have inflicted pain upon my<sup>saww</sup> neck. Which thing did you fear, that I<sup>saww</sup> have stood up to go to your slave girl?’
en.sarwar: 12. A group of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Once, the Holy Prophet, when he was with ‘A’ishah, during the night decided to perform optional Salah (prayer).

‘A’ishah woke up and searched around for him with her hand but did not find him. She thought he might have gone to her slave girl. She got up searching around and stepped on his neck when he was prostrating, weeping and saying, ‘(O Lord,) my person and my imagination have prostrated before You and my heart believes in You.
I come to You with bounties and confess my great sin. I have done a bad deed. I have done injustice to myself so forgive me; no one forgives a great sin except You.

I seek refuge with Your pardon from Your punishment, I seek refuge with Your pleasure from Your anger, I seek refuge with Your mercy from Your punishment and I seek refuge with You from You. I can never praise or admire You sufficiently. You are as You have praised Yourself. I ask forgiveness from You and turn to You in repentance.’
When he came back he asked, “A’ishah, why did you hurt my neck? Were you afraid that I might go to your slave girl?”’
